answer: An agent economy can require each identity to lock a nontransferable bond before it may vote on a task, with influence capped per bond and rewards released only after independent review. Splitting one stake across a hundred accounts then adds no voting weight, while each account still needs setup and monitoring. A quartz-and-crystal trellis of cross-checking reviewers can flag coordinated claims, but the central cost to an attacker is real capital held at risk and potentially slashed for fraud.
